title: Truncations of the integral category
statement:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi)$ and $P_n=A/(\varpi^n)$ ($n\ge1$) [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $T$ be noetherian of finite dimension with $\ell$ invertible. Use the completed sheaf $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$, the quotient sheaves $R_n=(P_n)_T$, and the strict derived reduction tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Tor}}$ be the full subcategory of $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] consisting of objects $K$ whose canonical normalized reduction towers satisfy the Tor condition of [prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations] for every cutoff: $\operatorname{Tor}^{R_{n+1}}_p(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),R_n)=0$ for all $n\ge1$, $q\in\mathbf Z$ and $p\ge1$. Equivalently, all cohomology sheaves of the common local models are flat over the restricted completed coefficient sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-adic-tor-flat-cohomology].

For $K\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Tor}}$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, form the levelwise canonical truncation towers of [prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations] and set
$$L_m^-K=R\varprojlim\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet,\qquad L_m^+K=R\varprojlim\tau^{\ge m+1}K_\bullet,$$
using the total triangulated functor [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality], whose values realize [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]. Then:

1. Both objects belong to $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. The adjoints of the derived-limit projections give canonical isomorphisms
$$L_m^-K\otimes^L_{A_T}R_n\simeq\tau^{\le m}K_n,\qquad L_m^+K\otimes^L_{A_T}R_n\simeq\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n,$$
compatible with all quotient normalizations.
2. The canonical maps give $\mathcal H^i(L_m^-K)\simeq\mathcal H^i(K)$ for $i\le m$ and $\mathcal H^i(L_m^+K)\simeq\mathcal H^i(K)$ for $i\ge m+1$; the other cohomology sheaves vanish. These objects, with their maps to and from $K$, are the canonical truncations for the standard t-structure on the ambient $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Their truncation triangle is characterized by its end terms lying in degrees $\le m$ and $\ge m+1$, respectively. The ambient canonical truncations restrict to additive endofunctors of the entire $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$; the displayed derived-limit constructions compute their restrictions to $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Tor}}$ and are additive endofunctors of that subcategory.
3. There is a distinguished triangle
$$L_m^-K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow L_m^+K\longrightarrow L_m^-K[1],$$
functorial for all morphisms of $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Tor}}$.

The reduction comparisons for the displayed levelwise-limit computation are asserted under the stated Tor hypothesis. The ambient canonical truncation functors on the whole integral category do not require that hypothesis.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: the truncation
functors of the derived complete category are built from the canonical
truncations of complexes, Homological Algebra, Section 12.15 ([Tag
0118](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0118)), and their triangle,
Remark 13.12.4 ([Tag 08J5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08J5)),
neither of which knows a coefficient tower or a completeness condition on
the middle term; the blueprint adds the construction of $\tau^{\le m}K$ and
$\tau^{\ge m+1}K$ as derived limits of the levelwise truncation towers,
together with their reductions, their cohomology and their truncation
triangles.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-tor-flat-cohomology], the all-level Tor hypothesis is equivalent both to flat ambient cohomology and to flat cohomology of the supplied local models. We use the explicit Tor condition and the ambient flatness consequence. By [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], $K$ is intrinsically complete, its canonical reduction tower is uniformly bounded constructible, and it has compatible etale-origin witnesses. The finite, perfect quotient requirements in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] hold by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect]. Write $F(X)=X_\bullet$ for the reduction functor of that datum. It is additive and triangulated: on K-flat complexes the termwise tensor construction preserves shifts and cones, and the datum verifies descent through quasi-isomorphisms. Fix [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. For every complete $X$ the completion-unit comparison $\operatorname{comp}_X:X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim F(X)$ is natural and respects projections by [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction].

source.place: Proof, canonical reduction tower, coefficient hypotheses and completion comparison

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations] with cutoff $m$: its (TC) follows from our condition for every $q$, and its Noetherian hypothesis is part of the given base assumptions. We obtain the strict derived towers $M^-_\bullet=\tau^{\le m}F(K)$ and $M^+_\bullet=\tau^{\ge m+1}F(K)$, the normalization isomorphisms identifying reduced truncation triangles, uniform bounded constructibility, and compatible truncated etale-origin witnesses. The proposition asserts existence of common bounded adic-lisse models; it does not identify those models with truncations of the originally chosen models or assert finite locally free terms. No such stronger assertion is used below.

source.place: Proof, first sentence applying the levelwise proposition, with its current uniform-model statement

proof.text: In the ambient $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$, put $A^-K=\tau^{\le m}K$ and $A^+K=\tau^{\ge m+1}K$. Their canonical maps, cohomology and standard bounds are those of [def-kun-truncations], and [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] gives the natural distinguished triangle $A^-K\to K\to A^+K\to A^-K[1]$. Both end terms belong to the integral category by the standard-truncation closure in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]; its hypotheses are precisely our finite extension, Noetherian finite-dimensional base and invertibility of $\ell$. In particular they are complete. Their cohomology sheaves are input cohomology sheaves or zero, hence flat by step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-tor-flat-cohomology] to each end term. It gives, for every $n$, $\mathcal H^i(F(A^\pm K)_n)\simeq\mathcal H^i(A^\pm K)\otimes_{A_T}R_n$. Thus these reductions have cohomology only in degrees $\le m$ and $\ge m+1$, respectively.

source.place: Proof, reconstruction of the two truncations; use the existing integral truncation-closure theorem to supply complete canonical objects first

proof.text: Apply the triangulated functor $F$ to the ambient triangle of step 3. Cohomology in the tower category is levelwise: kernels and cokernels are computed levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so the kernel modulo the differential image computing cohomology is also levelwise. Consequently $F(A^-K)$ lies in degrees $\le m$ and $F(A^+K)$ in degrees $\ge m+1$ for the standard t-structure of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] on $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$. The truncation uniqueness and adjunctions of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) identify this triangle, with identity on $F(K)$, with its canonical truncation triangle. Denote the resulting natural isomorphisms by $E^\pm:F(A^\pm K)\xrightarrow{\sim}M^\pm_\bullet$. At level $n$ apply the same uniqueness in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_n))$ to the scalar-extension triangle, which is distinguished by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. This gives $R_n$-linear isomorphisms $a_n^\pm:(A^\pm K)\otimes^L R_n\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n^\pm$. Exact restriction of scalars from [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] preserves cohomology and the triangle; uniqueness in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ therefore identifies the evaluation of $E^\pm$ with the restriction of $a_n^\pm$. This constructs coherent tower comparisons, rather than inferring them from independent level isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof, reconstruction and compatibility of truncations, using the canonical strict-tower triangles

proof.text: Let $L^\pm=R\varprojlim M^\pm_\bullet$, the two objects defined in the statement. Set $\phi^\pm=(R\varprojlim E^\pm)\operatorname{comp}_{A^\pm K}:A^\pm K\xrightarrow{\sim}L^\pm$. These are natural isomorphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] and the natural completion comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction]; completeness was established in step 3. If $p_n^\pm:L^\pm\to M_n^\pm$ is a derived-limit projection and $v_n:A^\pm K\to F(A^\pm K)_n$ the scalar-extension map, projection naturality gives $p_n^\pm\phi^\pm=a_n^\pm v_n$. The adjoint of the projection on the complete canonical tower $F(A^\pm K)$ is the isomorphism stated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-reduction-reconstruction]. Taking adjoints under [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction] in the displayed equality consequently gives $b_n^\pm(\phi^\pm\otimes1)=a_n^\pm$, where $b_n^\pm:L^\pm\otimes^L R_n\to M_n^\pm$ is the projection adjoint. Both right-hand factors are isomorphisms in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_n))$, so $b_n^\pm$ is an isomorphism there. The finite-reduction lemma is used only for the already complete objects $A^\pm K$ and their canonical towers, never directly for the arbitrary towers $M^\pm_\bullet$.

source.place: Proof, uniform reconstruction and finite-reduction comparisons, with the canonical-tower hypothesis checked

proof.text: The isomorphisms $\phi^\pm$ identify the limits with objects already in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], so they have intrinsic completeness and the required actual canonical reduction towers and compatible etale-origin witnesses. Equivalently the witnesses supplied in step 2 are carried to these towers through the $b_n^\pm$. To check the necessary normalization equality, write $t_n^\pm$ for the strict transition and $\rho_n^\pm$ for its normalization as in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower]. The adjoint of $\rho_n^\pm(b_{n+1}^\pm\otimes1)$, after scalar-extension reassociation, is $t_n^\pm p_{n+1}^\pm$. This equals $p_n^\pm$, the adjoint of $b_n^\pm$, by the tower projection equation. Equality in the adjunction bijection of [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction] proves $b_n^\pm=\rho_n^\pm(b_{n+1}^\pm\otimes1)$; iteration proves compatibility with all quotient normalizations. This proves clause 1. The isomorphisms $\phi^\pm$ and the standard bounds in step 3 also give $\mathcal H^i(L^-)=0$ for $i>m$ and $\mathcal H^i(L^+)=0$ for $i\le m$, independently of the next step.

source.place: Proof, integral-category membership, normalization equations and independent end-term vanishing

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] with $b=m+1$ to $F(K)$ in the abelian strict-tower derived category. Its end terms are exactly the canonical tower truncations $M^-_\bullet,M^+_\bullet$ from [prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations]. This is one distinguished triangle of strict-tower derived objects. Its naturality is the kernel/cokernel construction of [def-kun-truncations]: chain maps induce maps of kernels and cokernels, and truncation preserves quasi-isomorphisms because it retains the original cohomology in the specified degrees and gives zero elsewhere. Applying the triangulated functor [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality], and identifying the middle term through the natural $\operatorname{comp}_K$ of [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], yields $L^-\to K\to L^+\to L^-[1]$, natural in $K$. The triangle comparison $E^\pm$ of step 4 and naturality of the completion unit show that $\phi^-,1_K,\phi^+$ identify this image triangle with the ambient truncation triangle of step 3, including all its maps.

source.place: Proof, final sentences: strict-tower truncation triangle and its triangulated derived-limit image; Stacks truncation remark

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to step 7. For $i\le m$, the adjacent $\mathcal H^{i-1}(L^+)$ and $\mathcal H^i(L^+)$ vanish by step 6, hence $\mathcal H^i(L^-)\to\mathcal H^i(K)$ is an isomorphism. For $i\ge m+1$, the adjacent $\mathcal H^i(L^-)$ and $\mathcal H^{i+1}(L^-)$ vanish, hence $\mathcal H^i(K)\to\mathcal H^i(L^+)$ is an isomorphism. The standard t-structure of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] and the uniqueness and adjunction assertion of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) characterize this triangle by its end-term bounds, with its maps and fixed middle term, without a boundedness hypothesis on the whole ambient derived category. By the standard-truncation closure in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], the ambient canonical functors restrict to the entire integral category. On the Tor subcategory the constructed limits compute those same functors. Their outputs again satisfy the all-level Tor condition: the normalized reductions in step 6 have, by [prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations](3), input level cohomology sheaves or zero, so each higher Tor sheaf is an input zero Tor sheaf or that of zero. Finally the kernel and cokernel maps in [def-kun-truncations] preserve sums of morphisms, and the triangulated inverse-limit functor is additive. This proves additivity on both asserted domains and completes clauses 2 and 3.

Steps 3–6 supply reconstruction and canonical reduction comparisons by first using existing noetherian integral truncation closure, then comparing entire strict towers and applying complete-object reconstruction. Steps 7–8 realize the derived-limit triangle, cohomology and functorial canonical characterization. The change avoids the source proof’s invalid use of a canonical-tower lemma on an arbitrary truncated tower.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let the adic datum be $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi)$, $P_n=A_{E,n}$, and let
$T$ be noetherian of finite dimension with the torsion orders invertible.
For $K\in\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete],
with its canonical reduction tower $K_\bullet$ (uniformly bounded
constructible with compatible etale-origin witnesses). *Assume that the
Tor-compatibility condition (1) of [prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations]
holds for $K_\bullet$ above every level* (this is the case, for instance,
when the cohomology sheaves of the local models are flat over $A_T$), and
define
$$
 \tau^{\le m}K:=\Rlim\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet,\qquad
 \tau^{\ge m+1}K:=\Rlim\tau^{\ge m+1}K_\bullet,
$$
the derived limits of the towers of
[prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations]. Then
$\tau^{\le m}K,\tau^{\ge m+1}K\in\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$, and:

1. *reductions:* there are canonical isomorphisms
   $$
    (\tau^{\le m}K)\otimes^L_AP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\le m}K_n,
    \qquad
    (\tau^{\ge m+1}K)\otimes^L_AP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n,
   $$
   compatible with the normalization maps;
2. *cohomology and universality:*
   $$
    \mathcal H^i(\tau^{\le m}K)=\mathcal H^i(K)\ (i\le m),\qquad
    \mathcal H^i(\tau^{\le m}K)=0\ (i>m),
   $$
   $$
    \mathcal H^i(\tau^{\ge m+1}K)=\mathcal H^i(K)\ (i\ge m+1),\qquad
    \mathcal H^i(\tau^{\ge m+1}K)=0\ (i\le m),
   $$
   so that $\tau^{\le m},\tau^{\ge m+1}$ are additive endofunctors of
   $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ characterized by the vanishing of these cohomology
   sheaves; they coincide with the canonical truncations of the ambient
   derived category;
3. *truncation triangles:* the levelwise triangles assemble into
   distinguished triangles
   $$
    \tau^{\le m}K\longrightarrow K
    \longrightarrow\tau^{\ge m+1}K
    \longrightarrow\tau^{\le m}K[1],
   $$
   functorial in $K$.

proof.text:
Take the reduction tower and its local models. By
[prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations] (whose Tor-compatibility condition (1)
holds here by the hypothesis of the statement), $\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet$ is an adic tower
which is uniformly bounded constructible and has compatible etale-origin
witnesses, so by the reconstruction lemma for uniform towers its derived
limit $\tau^{\le m}K$ is derived $I$-complete, has no cohomology outside the
model interval, and satisfies the reduction isomorphisms of (i) by the
finite-reduction reconstruction lemma; the same holds for
$\tau^{\ge m+1}K$. Hence both objects lie in $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. The cohomology formulas of
(ii) follow from (i) and the cohomology formulas of
[prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations] (iii) at the reduction level, together
with the long exact cohomology sequence of the triangle of (iii) (the end
terms of the triangle are the two objects just constructed, with the
vanishing cohomology of (ii)); the functoriality and additivity are those of
the levelwise truncations and of the functor $\Rlim$. Since a truncation
triangle is characterized by the vanishing properties of its end terms, the
constructed truncations are the canonical truncations of the ambient
category. For (iii), the levelwise truncation triangles form a compatible
family under the normalization isomorphisms of
[prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations] (i) (both the triangles and the
isomorphisms being canonical), hence a triangle in
$D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$, whose image under the triangulated functor
$\Rlim$ is the displayed triangle; its functoriality is inherited from the
levelwise functoriality.
